cues.en: Instructor: Continuing on the discussion from the last video on measures of central tendency, now I'm going to start talking about the median.
cues.zh: 延續前一部的集中趨勢討論，現在開始談中位數。

cues.en: The median has a formula that looks like this.
cues.zh: 公式看起來像這樣。

cues.en: So you can see this formula is quite different from the mean.
cues.zh: 可以看到，和平均值公式很不同。

cues.en: In fact, the variable x, so we're computing the median of data set x, x doesn't even appear anywhere inside this formula, which may seem a little bit awkward at first.
cues.zh: 要算資料集x的中位數，但x甚至沒有出現在公式內部，一開始可能有點奇怪。

cues.en: So, but what this basically means, is we figure out how many data points are in total, and then we take the average of the data points, and that is the index corresponding to the median.
cues.zh: 基本上，先找出資料點總數，再取資料點的平均，那就是對應中位數的索引。

cues.en: And then, the value of the data set at that index is the median.
cues.zh: 資料集中，該索引位置的值，就是中位數。

cues.en: Now, that seems a little bit obtuse, so I just wanted to have this full formula in here.
cues.zh: 這說法有點拗口，只是想把完整公式放在這裡。

cues.en: But the easier way to explain this is that the median is just the middle value of the data.
cues.zh: 更簡單的解釋，是中位數就是資料的中間值。

cues.en: So the median is the data point in x, such that half of the data, so 50% of the data, is below that value and half the data, so 50% of the data,
cues.zh: x中的這個資料點，讓一半，也就是50%的資料低於它，另一半、50%的資料，

cues.en: is above that value.
cues.zh: 高於它。

cues.en: And that's the median.
cues.zh: 這就是中位數。

cues.en: It just literally cuts the data set exactly in half, into two equally sized halves.
cues.zh: 把資料集恰好切成大小相等的兩半。

cues.en: So the median is suitable for any distribution.
cues.zh: 中位數適合任何分布。

cues.en: Doesn't have to be Gaussian.
cues.zh: 不一定是高斯。

cues.en: It doesn't have to be normal, like with the mean.
cues.zh: 不像平均值，必須是常態。

cues.en: But the median is really only appropriate for unimodal distributions.
cues.zh: 但中位數真正適合的，是單峰分布。

cues.en: If you have multiple peaks in the distribution, then the median is still not going to be a really sensible, very useful measure of central tendency.
cues.zh: 若有多個峰，中位數仍不是合理、實用的集中趨勢量。

cues.en: And it is also most suitable for interval and ratio data.
cues.zh: 它也最適合區間與比率資料。

cues.en: So here is a numerical example.
cues.zh: 看個數字例子。

cues.en: So we have a data set containing five numbers.
cues.zh: 資料集有五個數。

cues.en: And what is the median?
cues.zh: 中位數是多少？

cues.en: So to compute the median, we have to sort the data values, so minus 2, 0, 1, 4, 7.
And then after the numbers have been sorted, then we take whatever is the value in the middle.
cues.zh: 排序後，取中間位置的值。

cues.en: So here you see the data values sorted, and then the median is the one in the middle.
cues.zh: 這是排序後資料，中位數就在中間。

cues.en: You can see in this simple example with a small data set that the median divides the sorted data into equal sized halves.
cues.zh: 小資料集的簡單例子，能看到中位數把排序資料切成相等兩半。

cues.en: So we have half the data below and half the data above.
cues.zh: 一半在下、一半在上。

cues.en: Now, unlike the mean, which has a more standardized notation, there isn't really a standard notation for median.
cues.zh: 不像平均值有較標準的記法，中位數沒有真正標準的記法。

cues.en: So people often will use something like this, med, or med, for median, and then the data set in a parentheses after this.
cues.zh: 常用像這樣，med，表示中位數，再在括號放資料集。

cues.en: Now this is an example for a data set with an odd number of points.
cues.zh: 這是奇數個資料點的例子。

cues.en: So then it's really easy to split it in the middle.
cues.zh: 很容易從中間切開。

cues.en: What do you do if you have an even number of points?
cues.zh: 偶數個資料點怎麼辦？

cues.en: Well, you have to adjust the formula slightly, but the concept is still the same.
cues.zh: 公式稍微調整，但概念相同。

cues.en: So essentially what you do is you still line up all the data, you sort the data according to their values from most negative to most positive.
cues.zh: 仍然將所有資料，依數值從最負到最正排序。

cues.en: And now in this case, there is no individual middle value.
cues.zh: 這時沒有單一中間值。

cues.en: So what we do is take the two values that are in the middle.
cues.zh: 就取中間的兩個值。

cues.en: So you can see we're still cutting up the data into an equal size below and an equal size above, but now it's two data points,
cues.zh: 仍然分成下面一半、上面一半，但現在取兩個資料點，

cues.en: and then we just compute the average of these two.
cues.zh: 再計算兩者平均。

cues.en: So the average of 1 and 4 is 2.5, so the median of this data set is 2.5.
cues.zh: 1與4的平均是2.5，所以資料集的中位數是2.5。

cues.en: And you can also see that if we put, you know, once we slice the median in here, then we're still dividing the data set into equal sized halves.
cues.zh: 把中位數插進這裡，仍把資料分成相等兩半。

cues.en: We have three data points to the left of the median and three data points to the right of the median, and that's the important part.
cues.zh: 中位數左邊三個資料點，右邊三個，這才重要。

cues.en: All right, so here's another failure scenario.
cues.zh: 再看另一個失敗例子。

cues.en: This is, or sorry, this is the failure scenario.
cues.zh: 抱歉，這邊才是失敗情況。

cues.en: Here we see a case where the median is appropriate because we have a unimodal distribution.
cues.zh: 這裡中位數適用，因為分布只有單峰。

cues.en: In fact, for normal distribution, the median and the mean will be basically the same.
cues.zh: 對常態分布而言，中位數與平均值基本相同。

cues.en: And this is a failure scenario, where, again, it's possible to compute the median.
cues.zh: 這則是失敗情況，仍然可以計算中位數。

cues.en: That's sort of mathematically, you know, we can compute the median, but the median is not a really useful measure of central tenancy
cues.zh: 數學上可以算，但中位數不是很有用的集中趨勢量，

cues.en: because this distribution has a lot of concentration of data points over here and over here, and actually very few data points are concentrated
cues.zh: 因為資料大量聚集這裡與這裡，反而很少資料聚在，

cues.en: around here, where the actual median is.
cues.zh: 真正中位數所在的這裡。

cues.en: So this median value is still splitting the data into two equal halves.
cues.zh: 中位數仍然將資料切成相等兩半。

cues.en: But the idea of interpreting the median is that it tells you something about where the data are most strongly clustered, and that's clearly not the case for this second distribution.
cues.zh: 但解讀中位數的用意，是告訴你資料最密集的地方；第二個分布顯然不是如此。

cues.en: So again, this is a case where the median is not really a very informative measure of central tendency.
cues.zh: 所以這是中位數不太有資訊價值的集中趨勢例子。

cues.en: All right, but here is a positive case.
cues.zh: 不過，這裡是正面的例子。

cues.en: This is a case where the median is actually outperforming the mean.
cues.zh: 這裡中位數的表現比平均值好。

cues.en: Remember this from the previous video.
cues.zh: 記得前一部影片。

cues.en: Here we have this lopsided distribution, or this right-skewed distribution.
cues.zh: 這是偏斜、右偏分布。

cues.en: And the mean is all the way out here, which actually is a little awkward, right?
cues.zh: 平均值遠在這裡，有點彆扭，對吧？

cues.en: Because this is not indicating anything special about the distribution, but the median is cutting the data in half.
cues.zh: 它沒有指向分布的特殊位置，但中位數把資料切成兩半。

cues.en: And so the median is actually much less sensitive to all of these outlying points, this pull of the distribution here.
cues.zh: 因此，中位數對這些離群點、分布被往外拉的現象，敏感度低很多。

cues.en: So in this case, the median is going to be much closer to the peak of the distribution compared to the mean.
cues.zh: 這時，中位數比平均值更接近分布峰。

cues.en: I'd like to show you a real world example of comparing the mean and the median to real world data.
cues.zh: 想用真實資料，展示比較平均與中位數的實際例子。

cues.en: These are data that I got from this website, Daily Kos.
cues.zh: 資料來自Daily Kos網站。

cues.en: And the point of these data is to show income distributions in the US in this blue line and in the Netherlands in this magenta line.
cues.zh: 藍線顯示美國收入分布，洋紅線顯示荷蘭。

cues.en: And so what you see also reported here is the median income and the average income.
cues.zh: 這裡也報告收入中位數與平均。

cues.en: And here's, well, the median and the the average income, so for the US and for the Netherlands.
cues.zh: 這裡是美國與荷蘭的中位數、平均收入。

cues.en: and what you see is that the US average is much higher than the median, whereas in the Netherlands, the median,
cues.zh: 可以看到，美國平均遠高於中位數；荷蘭的中位數，

cues.en: or sorry, the average is only a little bit higher than the median.
cues.zh: 抱歉，是平均值，只比中位數高一點。

cues.en: And so comparing these kinds of income distributions for the mean versus the median is actually one index of income inequality.
cues.zh: 所以比較收入分布的平均與中位數，其實是收入不平等的一項指標。

cues.en: And that is because if you imagine that there's no income inequality, or maybe very, very little income inequality, then the mean and the median are almost the same value
cues.zh: 想像沒有，或只有非常少的收入不平等，平均與中位數會幾乎相同，

cues.en: because there are most people earning roughly a similar amount of money and not so many people with really, really high incomes.
cues.zh: 因為大部分人收入大致相近，沒有很多人收入特別高。

cues.en: In contrast, when you have a lot of people with making a small amount of money and a small number of people making a huge amount of money, then that's going to pull up the average,
cues.zh: 相反地，很多人賺少量收入，少數人賺非常多，就會拉高平均，

cues.en: but it doesn't pull up the median quite as much.
cues.zh: 但不會那麼大幅拉高中位數。

cues.en: So this can be taken as one indicator that the US has more income inequality compared to the Netherlands.
cues.zh: 所以這可以當作美國收入不平等比荷蘭高的一項指標。

cues.en: So, real world example of comparing mean and median.
cues.zh: 這是比較平均與中位數的實際例子。

cues.en: So the last measure of central tendency that I'm going to introduce you to here is called the mode.
cues.zh: 最後介紹的集中趨勢量，叫眾數。

cues.en: Now this is a little bit confusing because earlier in the video about data distribution, so just a couple videos ago,
cues.zh: 這有點混淆，因為前幾部介紹資料分布時，

cues.en: I said that the mode of a distribution refers to how many peaks it has.
cues.zh: 說過分布的mode指有多少個峰。

cues.en: So we have a unimodal distribution, a bimodal distribution, a multimodal distribution.
cues.zh: 有單峰、雙峰、多峰分布。

cues.en: You can also have trimodal distributions.
cues.zh: 也有三峰分布。

cues.en: So this, unfortunately, the same term, but it means slightly different things.
cues.zh: 很不幸，是相同詞彙，但意思稍有不同。

cues.en: So I've discussed terminological confusion quite often in this course, so this, again, just something you have to get used to.
cues.zh: 課程裡常談術語混淆，這又是只能習慣的例子。

cues.en: Okay, so the mode of a data set is the most common value.
cues.zh: 資料集的眾數，就是最常見的值。

cues.en: It's suitable for any distribution, and it's also suitable for any data type, except that numerical data need to be converted.
cues.zh: 適用任何分布，也適用任何資料類型，但數值資料需要轉換。

cues.en: So interval or ratio data need to be converted into discrete data.
cues.zh: 區間與比率資料，需要轉成離散資料。

cues.en: That said, the mode is mostly used for nominal data.
cues.zh: 不過，眾數主要用於名目資料。

cues.en: It's most informative, it's most indicative for nominal type data.
cues.zh: 對名目資料，最有資訊、最具指示性。

cues.en: Okay, so let's see a numeric example.
cues.zh: 看個數字例子。

cues.en: Here we have a data distribution.
cues.zh: 這裡有資料分布。

cues.en: So what you do to compute the mode is basically just count the number of unique elements in there.
cues.zh: 計算眾數，基本上先找出唯一元素。

cues.en: And you count the number of elements that have a value of each unique element.
cues.zh: 再計算每個唯一值，出現多少次。

cues.en: So there's two 0s, there's three 1s, and there's one of each of these things.
cues.zh: 有兩個0、三個1，其他值各一個。

cues.en: So the mode is the most common value, so in this case, it's number 1.
cues.zh: 眾數是最常見的值，所以這裡是1。

cues.en: Now, one interesting property of the mode, which you don't have with the mean or the median, is that it's actually possible to have two modes of a distribution.
cues.zh: 眾數有個平均值、中位數沒有的有趣性質：一個分布可以有兩個眾數。

cues.en: So for example, let's imagine this data set.
cues.zh: 例如這個資料集。

cues.en: All I did was put in another 0.
cues.zh: 只是多放一個0。

cues.en: So there's still only one of 2, 3 and 4, but now there's three 0s and there's three 1s.
cues.zh: 2、3、4仍各一個，但現在有三個0、三個1。

cues.en: So in fact, this distribution has two modes.
cues.zh: 所以這個分布有兩個眾數。

cues.en: It has a mode at 0 and has a mode at 1.
cues.zh: 0是眾數，1也是。

cues.en: So two equally valid modes of this distribution.
cues.zh: 是兩個同樣有效的眾數。

cues.en: The mode of a normal distribution is actually still its peak value.
cues.zh: 常態分布的眾數，仍然是峰所在的值。

cues.en: This is the value that has the most number of occurrences.
cues.zh: 這是出現次數最多的值。

cues.en: Now, what's interesting about the mode is that for this kind of bimodal distribution, it's actually possible, in theory, it's possible, to have the mode be really the correct measures
cues.zh: 有趣的是，對這種雙峰分布，理論上可以讓眾數，成為真正正確的，

cues.en: of central tendencies of this distribution.
cues.zh: 集中趨勢量。

cues.en: Now of course, if these are real data, the the chance, you know, that you're going to get exactly the same number of data values, exactly the same count for this bin
cues.zh: 當然，如果是真實資料，這個區間與，

cues.en: and that bin, isn't terribly high, but it is theoretically possible to have these two values be the mode.
cues.zh: 那個區間剛好出現完全相同次數的機會不高，但理論上可能兩者都是眾數。

cues.en: In practice, though, it's likely to be one of these two will be the mode.
cues.zh: 實務上，大概其中一個會是眾數。

cues.en: Here you see an example of where the mode is the most informative measure of central tendency of a distribution.
cues.zh: 這是眾數最能描述分布集中趨勢的例子。

cues.en: So this we've seen before.
cues.zh: 之前看過。

cues.en: How do most people get the news?
cues.zh: 多數人如何取得新聞？

cues.en: These are nominal data.
cues.zh: 這是名目資料。

cues.en: We can't really average, we can't take the median, but the mode is very informative.
cues.zh: 不能真正取平均或中位數，但眾數很有資訊。

cues.en: We can say that the mode, the modal method of people getting the news, or the medium that people use to get the news, is the internet.
cues.zh: 可以說，人們取得新聞最常用、眾數所對應的媒體，是網路。

cues.en: So that makes a lot of sense. That's the central tendency.
cues.zh: 很合理，這就是集中趨勢。

cues.en: The mode is the central tendency of this data set here.
cues.zh: 眾數是這個資料集的集中趨勢。

cues.en: And here's another example that we've seen.
cues.zh: 再看另一個之前見過的例子。

cues.en: This is the height of king penguins.
cues.zh: 國王企鵝的身高。

cues.en: And the mode is whichever bar has the most number of counts, or, you know, the highest percentage, so that's also here.
cues.zh: 眾數就是次數最多、或百分比最高的長條，也在這裡。

cues.en: Now, in this case, I would say you probably don't need to compute the mode.
cues.zh: 這裡大概不需要算眾數。

cues.en: It's a little awkward to compute the mode.
cues.zh: 算眾數稍微彆扭。

cues.en: It's correct. It's still a good measure of central tendency.
cues.zh: 它正確，仍是好的集中趨勢量。

cues.en: But here, for a distribution like this, you would probably want to go with the mean or the median.
cues.zh: 但這類分布，大概會選平均值或中位數。

cues.en: All right, so here's a summary of the three measures of central tendency from the previous video and this one.
cues.zh: 整理前一部與這部的三個集中趨勢量。

cues.en: So the mean, which is also called the average value, is the most commonly used measure of central tendency.
cues.zh: 平均數，也就是平均值，是最常使用的集中趨勢指標。

cues.en: However, it is very sensitive to outliers.
cues.zh: 但對離群值非常敏感。

cues.en: You'll see this in the code in a few videos from now.
cues.zh: 再過幾部的程式碼會看到。

cues.en: The median is the middle value.
cues.zh: 中位數是中間值。

cues.en: It's the value in the data that essentially cuts the data in half, such that 50% of the data values are smaller than the median and 50% of the data values are larger than the median.
cues.zh: 基本上將資料切成兩半，50%小於中位數，50%大於中位數。

cues.en: The the median is most common, or it's most useful for distributions that have one peak, but that are not normally distributed.
cues.zh: 中位數最常見，或最適合只有一個峰，卻不是常態的分布。

cues.en: If you have normally distributed or Gaussian distributed data use the mean.
cues.zh: 若為常態、高斯資料，用平均值。

cues.en: If you have a distribution with one peak, but with a non-normal distribution or strong outliers, then the median is most appropriate.
cues.zh: 若只有一個峰，但非常態，或有強烈離群值，中位數最適當。

cues.en: And the mode is simply the most common value, and that's most appropriate for nominal data types.
cues.zh: 眾數只是最常出現的值，最適合名目資料。

cues.en: So three measures of central tenancy.
cues.zh: 這就是三個集中趨勢量。

cues.en: This is really important.
cues.zh: 非常重要。

cues.en: These are like the foundations of descriptive statistics along with measures of dispersion that you will learn about soon.
cues.zh: 加上稍後學習的離散程度量，它們就是敘述統計的基礎。
